conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that based on high-quality clinical evidence, ivermectin does not lower the risk of death in COVID-19 patients and is ineffective for treating or preventing the disease. Therefore, it clearly rejects the claim.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
Based on high-quality clinical evidence, **ivermectin does not lower the risk of death in COVID-19 patients**. 

While early observational studies and unvetted meta-analyses suggested a potential benefit, rigorous randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews have consistently shown that ivermectin is ineffective for treating or preventing COVID-19.

### Summary of Evidence

* **Cochrane Systematic Reviews:** Comprehensive Cochrane reviews analyzing randomized controlled trials found no reliable evidence to support using ivermectin to treat COVID-19 or lower mortality rates (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD015017_ivermectin-preventing-and-treating-covid-19).
* **Meta-Analyses of RCTs:** A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 randomized clinical trials involving over 7,000 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients concluded that ivermectin did not reduce all-cause mortality, hospital stay durations, or viral clearance compared to placebo or standard care (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0924857924001663).
* **Major Randomized Trials:** Large clinical studies, such as the TOGETHER trial, showed that ivermectin failed to reduce hospital admissions or severe illness progression in outpatients diagnosed with COVID-19 (https://www.drugs.com/ivermectin.html).
* **Methodological Issues in Early Claims:** Researchers noted that early meta-analyses and reports claiming dramatic reductions in mortality suffered from significant methodological limitations and risks of bias (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353521706_Ivermectin_for_preventing_and_treating_COVID-19).

Major health organizations, including the World Health Organization (WHO) and the U.S. FDA, recommend against using ivermectin for COVID-19 outside of approved clinical trials.
